title: spawnRailedChild's railsEntry option can put any test's child in fork mode, which turns off the general non-loopback deny for that child
severity_rationale: S4 hygiene: it is a test-code option, not an env var or flag, so it is not a bypass under NAC-05. A fork-mode child's env is still sentinels, its .env and data blocks and DB tripwire are still installed, and Telegram is still denied. It could reach the general network only if a test passed a real URL literally.

evidence.note: the option is limited to the two entries but not restricted by caller
the fork entry installs mode fork, where only Telegram is denied
used only by childRails.test.ts and hardhatChildEnv.test.ts, both rail proofs

sibling_sites_checked: Every other spawnRailedChild option was checked in judgment-reviews.json (inheritedEnv, envOverrides, homeOverride, nodeOptions, ledgerRunId, cwd, withVitestEnv). This is the only option that changes which rail mode a child gets. The module header names it ("which rails entry preloads") but does not list it as a limit.
recommendation: Extend the spawn-site gate so railsEntry: setup-fork is accepted only in the rail proof test files, in the same way the computed-require allowance is limited.
